figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of BRIDGE. DFGE constructs dual-frequency graph evidence; BEN computes normalized behavior support; CRI integrates the residual only inside the selected candidate set.

Table 1: Overall recommendation performance on three Amazon datasets. All methods use the same processed splits, BEIT3 features, and full-sort evaluation protocol. BRIDGE is selected by best validation Recall@20 under the same setting. Results of the strongest baselines and our method are reported with mean ± standard deviation over 5 random seeds. ∗∗ denotes statistical significance at 𝑝 < 0.01 under independent two-sample 𝑡-test against the best baseline.

Figure 2: Representation-spectral frequency diagnostic on Amazon Baby. Error bars denote the observed ranges. Leading singular-energy bands are more cross-view consistent, while later bands retain stronger ranking signal than the leading bands but remain insufficient as a standalone ranker. This is an SVD ordering in the learned latent space, not a Laplacian eigenmode plot.
Figure 3: Compact interpretability controls for BRIDGE. BEN evidence opens CRI and produces local corrections; BRIDGE also shifts exposure while improving mid, tail, and cold recall.
Table 2: Core Baby ablations and cross-dataset residual alternatives. All rows use the same splits, BEIT3 features, candidate restriction, and full-sort evaluation protocol.
Table 3: Candidate-side controls on Amazon Baby, Sports, and Electronics. To keep the control study in the main text, we report the primary Recall@20 and NDCG@20 metrics.

Table 4: Popularity-stratified diagnostic and exposure track. Head, Mid, Tail, and Cold report Recall@20 within each itempopularity stratum; Head Exp. is the top-20 exposure share assigned to head items.
